preamble: T has the same meaning throughout

clue.text: They provided Henry VIII with cash, without flower

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the cash word wraps round the flower

parts.note: monies is a formal word for sums of cash
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A history note: Henry VIII's cash came from somewhere that had no flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads on into 'cash', so the clue is close to an &lit: Henry VIII dissolved the monasteries and took their wealth. 'Without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's Dissolution seized the wealth and lands of England's religious houses, filling the royal treasury.

clue.text: Hogarth's composed, including rights, one-time massacre scene

indicators.note: including means the word for composed holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: composed, as in made up or created, gives made
R is short for right, so two Rs stand for rights
the Roman numeral for one is I
an age is a long period of time
the Alamo in Texas was the scene of the 1836 massacre of its defenders

explanation.surface: A Hogarth painting depicting a massacre, with rights included somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' looks like 'former' but splits into I and AGE. Hogarth's series is known by its French title, so 'Hogarth's' alone names it.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth painted a famous satirical series of six pictures under this French title about a fashionable match.

clue.text: King leaves Kenyan town for island republic

indicators.note: leaves means the king's letter goes away from the town name

parts.note: Nakuru is a town in Kenya's Rift Valley
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch departs a town in Kenya to go to an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny independent island nation in the Pacific, a republic since 1968.

clue.text: T to climb for one without leader

parts.note: to scale a wall is to climb it

indicators.note: without leader means the word one loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone must climb on behalf of a person who has no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says T means the same throughout: it stands for TRIANGLE, so this T is a kind of triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle is one whose three sides are all of different lengths.

clue.text: T for bird that's drunk ale outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled drink goes round the bird
drunk suggests the letters of ale are befuddled into a new order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird that has drunk ale stands in for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives EAL from ALE, which goes outside TERN. T is TRIANGLE: the eternal triangle is the classic love triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The eternal triangle is the stock romantic situation of two people rivals for a third.

clue.text: Essential T needs altering

indicators.note: needs altering says the letters of the word T stands for must be rearranged

parts.note: the preamble makes T stand for triangle throughout

explanation.surface: An essential item requires some alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs altering' rearranges TRIANGLE, the word T stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is essential, forming a necessary part of the whole.

clue.text: All must be sat in a play that's not a mere taster

indicators.note: play means the preceding letters are rearranged, as in at play

parts.words: All must be sat in a

explanation.surface: Everyone has to sit in a theatre production that is more than a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the stage show everyone is sitting in; it is the anagram signal, and 'in a' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty, filling meal is the opposite of a small taster or nibble.

clue.text: Sailor queen over sisters?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
Good Queen Bess was Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A sailor's queen ranks above her sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: BESS is the pet name of Queen Elizabeth I. The question mark marks 'sisters' as nuns, not siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent is set over the nuns, who are known as sisters.

clue.text: Locker at flat remote, for example?

parts.note: a key is something that locks
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A locker at a remote flat, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote control is one example of a small panel of buttons for entering commands.

clue.text: T, like the rig?

definitions.meaning: T stands for triangle: the ... Triangle is the Atlantic region of lost ships
a sailing rig with a tall triangular mainsail

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings use the Atlantic island's name: a notorious triangle of sea and a style of yacht rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is famous for vanishings, and a Bermuda rig is a type of sail plan.

clue.text: Early start aboard with the food

indicators.note: start means just the opening letter of early is taken

parts.note: split as a board, and a board can be a table, giving a table

explanation.surface: Getting on board early with the food supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' must be read as 'a board', a board being a table set for meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eatables, or an eatable, means something fit to eat: provisions.

clue.text: Lengthy work, a rune, translated by a lover of luxury

parts.note: an epic is a long poem or story

indicators.note: translated means the letters of a rune are turned into something else

explanation.surface: A long saga with a rune in it, rendered by a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is devoted to fine food and pleasure, so the adjective-noun describes a sensualist.

clue.text: Rise with rig

definitions.meaning: an outfit, rig being slang for clothing

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to stand or rise; as a noun it is an outfit or costume.

clue.text: Don't talk about one good enough to express regret

indicators.note: about means the hushing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about someone good enough to voice regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out audibly in sorrow is a way to show regret.

clue.text: Grade put back for the scholarly, as deserved

indicators.note: put back means the name is written backwards

parts.note: Lew Grade was a British television impresario
learned means scholarly

explanation.surface: A school grade moved back for the academic, as merited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grade' looks like a mark; it is Lew Grade, the British TV mogul, whose first name reversed gives WEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-earned has been fully merited by effort.

clue.text: Italian suite (say), endlessly adapted to accommodate single male

annotationWithheld.why: Italian suite (say), endlessly adapted to accommodate single male: the definition 'Italian suite (say)' (Italian sweet) needs 'suite', which is also the fodder SUIT(e) around I RAM, so 'suite' does two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Italian suite (say), endlessly adapted to accommodate single male

clue.text: On front page a weird mission shortened as pages

parts.note: the front page is page one, P plus I

indicators.note: weird signals that the letters of mission are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange mission written up in brief on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened as pages' is the definition: both pianissimo and pages abbreviate to pp. 'weird' turns MISSION into NISSIMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction meaning very softly is written pp, the same abbreviation as pages.

clue.text: European refinement

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the nationality adjective for Poland; the other is sophistication or finish.

clue.text: German magazine, say, and what's said about it?

indicators.note: about it means the patter word wraps round the example abbreviation

parts.note: a spiel is patter, what someone says
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A German periodical, and the talk surrounding it.
explanation.walkthrough: Der Spiegel is a leading German news weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Der Spiegel, meaning The Mirror, is Germany's best-known weekly news periodical.

clue.text: Like the fairies' ill meeting (Milton's Mad About Love)

indicators.note: about means the jumbled name goes round the zero
mad means the letters of Milton are crazily jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bracketed literary title about Milton going mad for love beside fairy lore.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon greets Titania with 'Ill met by moonlight' in A Midsummer Night's Dream. 'Mad' turns MILTON into MONLIT, and 'About' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy king and queen quarrel under the moon, so their unhappy meeting was lit by it.

clue.text: Backward female

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is rear, as in hind legs; the other is a female red deer.

clue.text: Refrain from Spades is Trumps

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A bridge player holds back because spades are trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to stop or hold back from doing something.

clue.text: Carrier left by religious leader

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist teacher

explanation.surface: A carrier abandoned by a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American animal is used as a pack beast to carry loads.

clue.text: One appeal for over half heavenly T

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
SOS is a distress call, an appeal for help

indicators.note: over half means the first five of the nine letters are kept, a little more than half the word

parts.note: celestial means heavenly

explanation.surface: A single appeal for more than half of a heavenly thing.
explanation.walkthrough: T is TRIANGLE. CELESTIAL keeps its first five of nine letters, more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle has two sides of equal length.

clue.text: Very sad — beheaded, rejected and set alight, it may be

indicators.note: rejected in a down clue means the remaining letters are turned back
beheaded means the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: tragic means very sad

explanation.surface: Something very sad: a beheading, a rejection, and a burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' leaves RAGIC from TRAGIC, and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is lit at one end to be smoked.

clue.text: Make love without success coming down from heaven?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the kissing word wraps the victory

parts.note: to snog is to kiss and cuddle
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A failed romance that falls from the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOG is British slang for a long kiss. 'Without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is falling from the sky, so the weather is coming down from above.

clue.text: Drunk as a snake?

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely drunk, and literally lacking legs like a serpent.

clue.text: Horses (from the play) in due course at a pound a T

parts.note: Equus is Peter Shaffer's play, and equi is the Latin plural for horses
later means in due course
L stands for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Horses from a stage show, eventually priced at a pound a time.
explanation.walkthrough: T is TRIANGLE. Equus is a Peter Shaffer play.
explanation.definitionFit: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal.
